name: Boiled tapioca with sesame salt
summary: Boiled cassava at the tunnels. The Ho Chi Minh City Tourism Promotion Center serves it with sesame salt and hot tea and calls it complimentary. Tuổi Trẻ, on 5 May 2024, says salt, and does not say sesame or tea.
origin: The tunnels at Củ Chi. The Ho Chi Minh City Tourism Promotion Center places it at the underground Hoàng Cầm kitchen. Tuổi Trẻ places boiled cassava dipped in salt on the relic.
howToEat: The Ho Chi Minh City Tourism Promotion Center says eat it with hot tea at the Hoàng Cầm kitchen, and says it is complimentary.
Tuổi Trẻ, on 5 May 2024, says boiled cassava dipped in salt, a wartime snack on the relic. It does not say sesame, tea, or complimentary.
Khu di tích lịch sử Địa đạo Củ Chi, in the 2021 reopening notice, names specialties at Chợ Quê and does not name tapioca. A clock for the kitchen was not printed. Check on arrival.
where: The Hoàng Cầm kitchen on the relic, on the tourism center account. Which gate was not printed. Tuổi Trẻ places the salt version on the relic and prints no gate.
priceBand: Complimentary, on the Ho Chi Minh City Tourism Promotion Center account. Tuổi Trẻ prints no price.
seoTitle: Boiled tapioca at the Cu Chi tunnels
seoDescription: Boiled cassava on the relic. Sesame salt and hot tea, called complimentary, on the tourism center account. Tuổi Trẻ says salt.
taste: The tourism center names sesame salt and hot tea. Tuổi Trẻ names salt. Both stay. Neither describes a further flavor.
